quotes: Seven patients (4 females, and 3 males) born in unrelated families, one of them consanguineous (first cousins), were affected by peculiar facies and gestures while smiling and crying, and by hydronephrosis, hydroureter and intravesical stenosis of the ureter

abnormal caliber of the urether in the prostatic and membranous portions, urethral valves, abnormal bladder with trabeculation, and diverticula associated with severe hypertrophy of the mucosa with sclerotic changes

records.label: 36 children with urofacial syndrome

phenotypes.text: inversion of facial expression when laughing

quotes: Between 1965 and 1986 we saw 36 children with enuresis and urinary tract infection in association with "inversion" of facial expression when laughing.
Urologic work-up of these patients disclosed characteristic findings of mild neuropathic bladder in all cases, with severe urinary tract damage in most of them.
About two thirds of the patients also had moderate to severe constipation.

records.label: 31 UFS patients
records.segregation: All 31 patients homozygous for D10S1726 and D10S198 vs 12% of unaffected relatives
quotes: The patients present with enuresis, urinary-tract infection, hydronephrosis, and voiding dysfunctions as a result of neurogenic bladders.

All 31 patients were found to be homozygous for two closely linked markers (D10S1726 and D10S198) located approximately 5 cM telomeric to D10S677, whereas only 12% of the unaffected relatives were homozygous for both markers (P < 10(-19)).

records.label: Turkish patient with urofacial syndrome
quotes: We report the first published case of urofacial syndrome in Turkey. The patient was diagnosed at 16 years of age, after having been followed with the diagnosis of recurrent urinary tract infection and vesico-ureteral reflux.

quotes: We report 11 patients with urofacial syndrome in five families from Turkey with a median follow up of 32 months (range, 2-44 months).
is a rare autosomal recessive condition that occurs in both genders and characterized by uropathy and facial abnormalities

notes.statement: Daly et al. (2010) described urofacial syndrome as a rare autosomal recessive disease characterized by facial grimacing when attempting to smile and failure of the bladder to void completely despite no anatomical outflow obstruction or overt neurologic damage; affected individuals often have reflux of infected urine to the upper renal tract, with risk of kidney damage and renal failure.
quotes: Urofacial syndrome (UFS) is a rare autosomal recessive disease characterized by facial grimacing when attempting to smile and failure of the urinary bladder to void completely despite a lack of anatomical bladder outflow obstruction or overt neurological damage.
UFS individuals often have reflux of infected urine from the bladder to the upper renal tract, with a risk of kidney damage and renal failure.

notes.statement: By whole-genome SNP mapping in one affected individual, Daly et al. (2010) defined a 16-Mb autozygous region on chromosome 10q23-q24 containing HPSE2.
quotes: Whole-genome SNP mapping in one affected individual defined an autozygous region of 16 Mb on chromosome 10q23-q24, within which a 10 kb deletion encompassing exons 8 and 9 of HPSE2 was identified.

notes.statement: Daly et al. (2010) did not identify HPSE2 mutations in 4 additional UFS patients, indicating genetic heterogeneity.
quotes: Mutations were not identified in four additional UFS patients, indicating genetic heterogeneity.

notes.statement: Daly et al. (2010) showed that HPSE2 is expressed in the fetal and adult central nervous system, where it might be implicated in controlling facial expression and urinary voiding, and in bladder smooth muscle, consistent with a role in renal tract morphology and function.
quotes: We show that HPSE2 is expressed in the fetal and adult central nervous system, where it might be implicated in controlling facial expression and urinary voiding, and also in bladder smooth muscle, consistent with a role in renal tract morphology and function.

notes.statement: Pang et al. (2010) noted that they had previously localized the urofacial syndrome gene to chromosome 10q24 by homozygosity mapping.
quotes: Previously, we localized the defective gene for the urofacial syndrome (UFS) to a region on chromosome 10q24 by homozygosity mapping.

notes.statement: Pang et al. (2010) identified loss-of-function mutations in the HPSE2 gene in all patients with urofacial syndrome studied, who came from Colombia, the United States, and France.
quotes: Mutations with a loss of function in the Heparanase 2 (HPSE2) gene were identified in all UFS patients originating from Colombia, the United States, and France.

notes.statement: Pang et al. (2010) noted that HPSE2 encodes a 592-amino acid protein with a domain homologous to the glycosyl hydrolase motif of heparanase (HPSE). They suggested that complete loss of HPSE2 function in UFS patients means HPSE2 may be important for the coordinated action of the muscles involved in facial expression and urine voiding.
quotes: HPSE2 encodes a 592 aa protein that contains a domain showing sequence homology to the glycosyl hydrolase motif in the heparanase (HPSE) gene
Complete loss of HPSE2 function in UFS patients suggests that HPSE2 may be important for the synergic action of muscles implicated in facial expression and urine voiding.

notes.statement: Derbent et al. (2009) described urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome as a rare autosomal recessive disorder featuring an 'inverted' facial expression, such that patients appear to cry when they smile, with serious urinary tract disorders resulting in enuresis, urinary tract infection, and hydronephrosis; some severely affected patients become hypertensive and progress to end-stage renal disease.
quotes: Urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome is a rare autosomal-recessive disorder that features an unusual "inverted" facial expression, such that patients appear to be crying when they smile.
The urinary issues usually result in enuresis, urinary tract infection, and hydronephrosis, and some severely affected patients become hypertensive and progress to end-stage renal disease.

notes.statement: Derbent et al. (2009) noted that the diagnosis may be missed because of variability of urinary problems and failure to recognize the characteristic facial grimacing, and recommended considering the syndrome in any patient with dysfunctional voiding, particularly in countries with high rates of consanguineous marriage.
quotes: though the diagnosis may be missed because of variability of these problems and failure to recognize the characteristic facial grimacing
Physicians should keep this syndrome in mind for any patient who presents with dysfunctional voiding, particularly in countries with high rates of consanguineous marriage.

notes.statement: Aydogdu et al. (2010) stressed that early diagnosis of urofacial syndrome is crucial for the management and prognosis of urinary problems caused by a dysfunctional bladder.
quotes: Early diagnosis is crucial for the management and prognosis of urinary problems due to a dysfunctional bladder.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2003) built a genomic sequence map covering the whole UFS interval on chromosome 10q23-q24. They narrowed the disease interval from about 360 kb to a 220-kb region containing the ACDP1 gene and part of the GOT1 gene. GOT1 had already been excluded as a candidate.
quotes: Our previous studies using homozygosity mapping have located the UFS gene to a genomic interval of approximately 360 kb on chromosome 10q23-10q24.
narrowed the disease interval to a genomic region of 220 kb that harbor the newly identified ACDP1 gene in addition to part of the GOT1 gene which has already been excluded as a candidate for UFS

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2003) searched the coding region, the 5-prime and 3-prime untranslated regions, the promoter region, and the exon/intron junctions of candidate genes in the 220-kb interval. They found no pathogenic mutation in UFS patients.
quotes: Extensive search for mutations in the coding region, the 5' and 3' untranslated regions, the promoter region, and the exon/intron junctions failed to identify a pathogenic mutation in UFS patients.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2003) concluded from their analyses that the same gene on chromosome 10q is responsible for all UFS patients from multiple ethnic groups.
quotes: our analyses indicated that the same gene on chromosome 10q is responsible for all UFS patients from multiple ethnic groups

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2003) described urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome as a rare disorder caused by a single recessive gene. It is characterized by congenital obstructive uropathy and an abnormal facial expression.
quotes: The urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome (UFS) characterized by congenital obstructive uropathy and abnormal facial expression is a rare disorder caused by a single recessive disease gene.

notes.statement: Garcia-Minaur et al. (2001) suggested that urofacial syndrome cases outside Colombia may be missed because of the variability of the urinary problems and failure to recognize the characteristic facial grimacing, and emphasized that early diagnosis has important consequences for the management and prognosis of the urinary problems.
quotes: It is likely that they may be missed because of variability of the urinary problems and failure to recognize the characteristic facial grimacing.
Establishing an early diagnosis has important consequences for the management and prognosis of urinary problems in these patients.

notes.statement: Garcia-Minaur et al. (2001) noted that urofacial syndrome was originally described in Colombian patients and that very few cases had been reported from other countries.
quotes: This entity was originally described in Colombian patients and very few cases have been reported from other countries.

notes.statement: Chauve et al. (2000) compared haplotypes in a French family with urofacial syndrome, the first European cases reported, with haplotypes previously described in patients from Colombia and America. The results were compatible with the same 10q23-q24 critical region and favored genetic homogeneity.
quotes: Haplotype analyses in our French family were compared with those previously described in patients from Columbia and America (literature data).
The results are compatible with the same localization of the critical region and favor the hypothesis of genetic homogeneity.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1999) built a physical map of the UFS critical region on 10q23-q24 and found new polymorphic markers there. Haplotype analysis with these markers placed the UFS gene within a single YAC clone of 1,410 kb.
quotes: We established a physical map and identified novel polymorphic markers in the UFS critical region. Haplotype analysis using the new markers mapped the UFS gene within one YAC clone of 1,410 kb.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1999) used homozygosity mapping in American patients of Irish heritage to show that the syndrome maps to the same 10q23-24 region as in the Colombian families, which shows genetic homogeneity.
quotes: Previously, we mapped the gene to a genomic interval of approximately 1 cM on chromosome region 10q23-24, using families from Columbia. Here we demonstrate genetic homogeneity of the syndrome through homozygosity mapping in American patients with Irish heritage.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1999) placed the glutamate oxaloacetate transaminase gene (GOT1) precisely within the new UFS critical region and worked out its genomic structure. Mutation analysis excluded GOT1 as the UFS gene.
quotes: We also determined the precise location of the gene encoding for glutamate oxaloacetate transaminase (GOT1) within the new UFS critical region and determined its genomic structure. However, mutation analysis excluded GOT1 as a candidate for the UFS gene.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1999) described urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome as a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by abnormal facial expression and urinary abnormalities.
quotes: The urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome (UFS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by abnormal facial expression and urinary abnormalities.

notes.statement: By a genome screen combining homozygosity mapping and DNA pooling in 20 patients, Wang et al. (1997) found D10S677 linked to and associated with urofacial syndrome (excess homozygosity in patients, P < 10(-6)). Haplotype analysis showed all 31 patients homozygous for D10S1726 and D10S198, about 5 cM telomeric to D10S677, versus 12% of unaffected relatives (P < 10(-19)), and recombinations placed the gene within a 1-cM interval between D10S1433 and D10S603 on chromosome 10q23-q24.
quotes: After analyses of 36 randomly chosen markers, D10S677 was identified as being linked to and associated with UFS, as suggested by a significant excess of homozygosity in patients compared with that in unaffected relatives (P < 10(-6))
These recombinational events place the UFS gene near D10S1726/D10S198 and within a 1-cM interval defined by D10S1433 and D10S603 on chromosome 10q23-q24.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (1997) described urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome as a rare autosomal recessive disease characterized by congenital obstructive uropathy and abnormal facial expression, with enuresis, urinary tract infection, hydronephrosis, and voiding dysfunction due to neurogenic bladder.
quotes: The urofacial (Ochoa) syndrome (UFS) is a rare autosomal recessive disease characterized by congenital obstructive uropathy and abnormal facial expression.

notes.statement: Ochoa and Gorlin (1987) concluded that the occurrence of the disorder in multiple sibs with normal parents, increased parental consanguinity, and an equal sex ratio indicated autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: The occurrence of the disorder in multiple sibs, normal parents, increased parental consanguinity, and equal sex ratio indicate autosomal recessive inheritance.

notes.statement: Ochoa and Gorlin (1987) proposed the term urofacial syndrome and stated that the association of inverted facial expression with neuropathic bladder and resulting genitourinary damage should prompt urologic evaluation of individuals with 'inversion' of facial expression.
quotes: The clear association of distortion in facial expression and neuropathic bladder with resultant damage to the genitourinary tract should prompt urological evaluation of individuals with "inversion" of facial expression.
We suggest the term urofacial syndrome for this disorder.

notes.statement: From genetic analysis of 3 families, one of them consanguineous (first cousins), Elejalde (1979) concluded that the condition is probably autosomal dominant with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance.
quotes: The genetic analysis of these families indicates that the condition is probably autosomal dominant, with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance.

notes.statement: Elejalde (1979) proposed that the syndrome reflects altered development of the facial and urinary developmental fields. The authors noted that the peculiar facies allows the condition to be recognized early, which can help early assessment and treatment and may lead to a better prognosis.
quotes: The syndrome represents alteration of facial and urinary developmental fields. The peculiar facies allows early recognition of the condition, and this can be helpful for early assessment and treatment, leading perhaps to a better prognosis.
